name: Emerging market currency momentum

origin.source_title: Currency momentum strategies (Journal of Financial Economics 106(3), 660-684)

how_it_works.simple: Among emerging market currencies, buy the ones that rose most over the past few months and sell the ones that fell most.
how_it_works.analogy: Like backing the players on a hot streak in a league where few scouts are watching.
how_it_works.precise: Rank currencies by past excess return over a formation window (1 to 12 months), long winners, short losers, hold one month. Menkhoff et al. find spreads up to about 10% a year before costs across up to 48 currencies, falling to about 4% after full spreads for the best version, and basically nothing among developed currencies after costs.

rule: Monthly: rank EM currencies by past 3-month return, long the top third, short the bottom third, equal weights, hold one month.
data_needed: Daily EM spot rates (ECB reference rates)
EM short-term interest rates for carry credit
economic_rationale: Limits to arbitrage: high costs and country risk in minor currencies keep slow-moving trends from being traded away.
why_it_might_fail: The return lives where costs are highest, so a realistic spread may consume it; the developed-market version already failed in our tests (EXP-0004).

reported_results.source: Menkhoff, Sarno, Schmeling and Schrimpf (2012), JFE, best strategy after full spreads
reported_results.notes: Quote: "returns for the best strategy (with f, h=1) drop from nearly 10% to about 4% p.a." after full spreads. Developed only: "basically non-existent after transaction costs".

relevance.reason: Tests directly why our G10 momentum failed; costs are the main risk.

research.notes: Added from RES-0012 and RES-0013 on 2026-10-21.
